record_identity.title: Deepfake of Western Australia Premier Roger Cook used in investment scam

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Deepfake of Western Australia Premier Roger Cook used in investment scam
incident_identity.date_basis: ABC News reported the Western Australian government warning on 8 November 2025.

summary: A fraudulent YouTube advertisement used an AI-generated likeness and voice of Western Australian Premier Roger Cook to promote an investment scheme as government-backed. Cook and the Western Australian Consumer Protection Commissioner rejected the endorsement and warned that the advertisement was fraudulent; the reporting reviewed for this record did not identify any realised victim loss. A member of the public alerted Consumer Protection on 7 November 2025. The team requested removal from the domain holder; Cook publicly denied endorsement the following day.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: ABC News preserved the government's warning and described a YouTube pop-up advertisement that imitated Roger Cook's appearance and voice. The Premier and Consumer Protection Commissioner rejected the endorsement and warned that the material was fraudulent. The reviewed evidence does not establish a realised victim loss. ABC dates the public alert to Friday 7 November and Cook’s response to the following day. The team requested removal; the article does not confirm removal or transaction prevention.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The synthetic advertisements falsely conveyed investment endorsement and concealed AI impersonation. The reported identity and agency failures are assessed separately from later framework versions. No realised victim loss is established.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case illustrates how synthetic public-office identity can be used to manufacture institutional credibility for fraud even where downstream monetary loss is not yet evidenced.
assessment_boundaries: No reviewed source establishes that a viewer transferred money or sustained financial loss.
The record does not infer how the advertisement was generated beyond the reported synthetic voice and likeness.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The advertisement used Roger Cook's synthetic likeness and voice as if they carried his real endorsement and public-office authority without his authority for that identity-bound portrayal.
AI-generated Roger Cook impersonation supplied false government endorsement to promote an investment scheme, materially reinforcing a deceptive economic solicitation.
A synthetic Roger Cook likeness and voice presented a fraudulent investment as government-backed, inviting a financial decision on false official authority.

The preserved evidence attributes the deceptive promotional objective and tactic to human operators using AI-generated material; it does not establish that an AI system selected or pursued its own objective through an agency-impairing tactic. The distinct synthetic-identity and solicitation mechanisms remain adjudicated under their applicable classes.
